program_meta.sop_limit: VERIFIED VERBATIM, EPFL Online Application page ('Statement of purpose' section): 'The statement of purpose should not exceed 1000 words. You are required to describe your academic background and your career strategy. Please be precise about the objectives you wish to reach through your studies at EPFL.' This CONFIRMS the prior note of a 1000-word cap - it is words, not characters, and it is the official current figure (source: https://www.epfl.ch/education/admission/admission-2/master-admission-criteria-application/online-application/, retrieved 2026-08-28). No separate page-count or character limit was found anywhere else on the official application pages.
program_meta.extra_essays: NOT STATED as a separate document. The application requires only: CV/resume, degree certificate(s), full transcripts, the one statement of purpose (1000 words, above), 3 referees' contact details, and ID/passport. No separate 'diversity statement' or 'personal history statement' analogous to the US model was found on the official Master's application pages.
program_meta.deadline_fall_2027: VERIFIED, two rolling windows per academic year (applies to intake starting September 2027, i.e. what EPFL calls its 'Master' cycle - EPFL does not publish deadlines by target calendar year the way US schools do; the same two windows recur annually). VERBATIM: 'Applications can be filled online from mid-November to the 15th of December, or from the 16th of December to the 31st of March.' Decisions: 'late March for applications registered by the 15th of December and mid-June for the applications registered by the 31st of March.' VISA NOTE, VERBATIM: 'People who need a visa are strongly advised to apply by the December deadline in order to have an answer earlier and have enough time for the visa procedure (which can take up to 3 months).' This resolves the prior 'not confirmed, similar Nov-Dec window' note: the December 15 deadline is real and is the one Akshat (needing a Swiss student visa) should target, not the March 31 deadline.
program_meta.lor_count: VERIFIED: Three (3) academic referees, confirmed VERBATIM: 'The contact details of three academic referees, who will each be asked to produce a recommendation letter for you... All other candidates are required to provide the contact details of three referees. The recommendation letters must be issued by professors who are aware of your work and achievements.' Hard floor: 'The application will not be processed if EPFL does not receive at least two reference letters.' So 3 are requested but only 2 must actually arrive for the application to be processed - still budget for 3. Letters are submitted directly by referees electronically; deadline is one week after the application deadline (exact date given in the applicant's confirmation email).
program_meta.gre: VERIFIED NOT REQUIRED / NOT EVEN A STANDARD OPTIONAL FIELD. VERBATIM (Online Application, 'Required documents'): 'Extra documents, such as TOEFL or GRE scores, research publications, or other portfolios of your previous work, are welcome but not compulsory.' This confirms the prior note - GRE is optional/supplementary only, never required, and can be omitted with no penalty implied by the page's wording.
program_meta.english_test: NOT STATED AS A FORMAL REQUIREMENT ON THE MASTER'S ADMISSION PAGES. The Online Application 'Required documents' list does not include a mandatory English test; TOEFL is explicitly listed only among the OPTIONAL 'extra documents... welcome but not compulsory.' The Computer Science program page states 'Excellent English language skills are required to follow this Master's program' (teaching language is English) but does not name a specific test, score, or exemption list - i.e. EPFL appears to assess English proficiency qualitatively via the dossier/transcripts/SOP rather than via a mandatory standardized test score for the MSc. This differs sharply from the Purdue/UMass/US-style hard TOEFL/IELTS cutoffs elsewhere in this file. India-specific exemption status: NOT STATED, because no mandatory test/exemption list exists to check against. CONFIDENCE: Medium - this is what the official pages say (or rather, do not say), but Akshat should double check the program-specific page and the online application portal itself for any hidden per-cycle requirement before assuming no test is needed.
program_meta.app_fee: VERIFIED VERBATIM (Online Application, 'Application fee'): 'CHF 150.- if you hold a foreign Bachelor's degree' (this is Akshat's case - Manipal/India). 'CHF 50.- if you hold a Bachelor's degree delivered by a Swiss HEU/UHS... or HES/FHS.' 'CHF 0.- if you hold a Bachelor's degree delivered by EPFL.' program_meta.faculty_directory_url: https://www.epfl.ch/schools/ic/about/faculty-members/ (full IC professor list, filterable by rank; downloadable xlsx also linked there); https://www.epfl.ch/research/faculty-members/ (EPFL-wide); https://www.epfl.ch/research/domains/cluster?field-of-research=Machine%20Learning%20%28ML%29 and similarly for 'Imaging and vision', 'Data science', 'Optimization' (EPFL's cross-school research-domain clusters, useful because several ML-relevant labs - e.g. LIONS, VITA - sit administratively in the School of Engineering STI, not in IC, despite doing core ML research).
program_meta.advisor_model: Master's-level: NOT an advisor-admission model. Admission is to the MSc CS program as a whole via the IC-wide dossier review described below; students choose courses/specializations and, in their final semesters, a semester project and Master's thesis lab placement (see ms_research_access). PhD-level (for later reference): EPFL runs PhDs through the EDIC doctoral school with a mix of direct faculty-driven admission and doctoral-school screening; not relevant to this MSc cycle but worth knowing that naming specific IC professors in the SOP is still the expected signal even though the MSc application itself is not routed to any individual professor.
program_meta.ms_research_access: STRUCTURALLY IMPORTANT AND UNDER-DOCUMENTED ON PUBLIC PAGES: EPFL's MSc CS is 120 ECTS with, in the final semesters, a mandatory semester project and a Master's thesis (typically 4-6 months), both of which are done inside a specific lab under a specific EPFL professor - this is the mechanism by which MSc students 'join a lab.' The exact placement process (application to a lab's open project list vs. direct cold-email to a professor vs. a centralized IC list of open semester-project topics) was NOT independently verified on an official page in this pass and should be confirmed via the IC 'Education' pages (https://www.epfl.ch/schools/ic/education/) or the study-plan PDF before Akshat writes his SOP - flag as NOT STATED / unverified pending a dedicated pass on IC semester-project logistics.
program_meta.notes: STRUCTURAL ADMISSION CONSTRAINT, QUOTED PRECISELY AS REQUESTED: the MSc CS 'Admission criteria' page states this program is 'consecutive to a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science... or Communication Systems... obtained at EPFL,' and for everyone else: 'Non-EPFL degrees: Bachelor's degrees obtained in the same fields but from another institution are eligible on the basis of an application dossier and must be accompanied by excellent academic records.' The Master admission-criteria & FAQ page reinforces this for non-Swiss-Bachelor's applicants generally: 'Anyone holding a Bachelor's degree from a university (or equivalent) in a field related to the EPFL curricula can apply... However, please be aware that admission is competitive. Only people with excellent academic records and references have good chances of being accepted.' In practice this means Akshat, holding a non-EPFL, non-Swiss Bachelor's, undergoes the FULL 'application dossier'-based case-by-case review described above, with no guarantee even if all listed prerequisites are met (contrast with EPFL-Bachelor's holders, who are auto-registered with no application at all) - this is the harder path referenced in the task brief, now quoted from the source. GRE/TOEFL are optional add-ons that 'are welcome' inside that same dossier, i.e. they can only help, never hurt, and can be omitted. Admission decision factors, VERBATIM: 'the quality of the application, the academic curriculum, the grades and results, the research references, and the area of specialization, as well as factors related to compliance with export-control and embargo legislation.' Two intake windows per cycle exist (mid-Nov-Dec 15 and Dec 16-Mar 31); Akshat should use the December 15 window given the 3-month Swiss student-visa lead time explicitly flagged by EPFL. Prerequisites for all applicants, VERBATIM: 'skills in mathematics, in particular in calculus, discrete mathematics, linear algebra and probability, as well as a solid understanding of algorithms, data structures, and databases are required... Candidates should be proficient in programming languages (Python, Java, or C++) and have experience in software development. Knowledge of operating systems, computer architecture, and the theory of computation is critical.' 'The acquisition of additional credits to fill any gaps may be required.' RED FLAG worth stating plainly: two of the six professors named in the user's own brief - Volkan Cevher (LIONS) and Alexandre Alahi (VITA) - are administratively in the School of Engineering (STI), not in IC (School of Computer and Communication Sciences), even though their labs are core ML research groups. LIONS was independently verified this pass (page confirms Cevher is actively supervising PhD defenses as of August 2026); VITA's page could not be fetched in this pass (rate-limited) and Alahi's current status is UNVERIFIED - flag as a gap. Fabio Nobile and Devis Tuia were checked against the retrieved IC faculty roster and are NOT on the IC list (Nobile is EPFL Mathematics/CSQI in SB; Tuia's ECEO group is at SB/ENAC, environmental remote sensing) - both are OUT OF SCOPE for an IC-routed MSc CS application and are not included below. Sabine Süsstrunk IS confirmed still listed as active Full Professor on the current IC roster (not emeritus) as of 2026-08-28.

faculty.research_areas: Generative modeling (diffusion models, flow matching, optimal transport) applied to molecular and cellular biology; learning from single-cell and imaging data; generative models for scientific discovery and perturbation prediction.

faculty.department: School of Computer and Communication Sciences (IC)
faculty.research_areas: Signal processing, graph signal processing/graph machine learning, image and video processing, adversarial robustness of deep networks, geometric deep learning.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's HiME work encodes structure (a label hierarchy) directly into the decoding rule rather than post-hoc; Frossard's long-running graph-signal-processing and geometric-deep-learning line is about encoding relational/structural priors directly into learning architectures, which is the same design philosophy applied to graphs instead of taxonomies. His group's adversarial-robustness and OOD work is also a plausible bridge to Akshat's A-PDF idea of a post-hoc plausibility filter on generated data.
